clue.text: Keen wrestling Oscar and I spice up

indicators.note: wrestlers grapple and twist each other about, so the words that follow are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic grappler announces they will add some zest to their bout with Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like an adjective describing the wrestler's attitude, but it is the definition in its sense of sharp-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen can mean mentally sharp and quick to notice, which is exactly what a perspicacious person is.

clue.text: Field of expertise of star, conceivably?

definitions.text: Field of expertise of star, conceivably?

blocks.note: surface reading: the professional domain in which a stage or screen star excels
setter's reading: the word star, when its letters are made to perform, can be turned into another word, which completes the phrase

explanation.walkthrough: The answer describes itself: PERFORMING ARTS is what a star works in, and performing (rearranging) STAR gives ARTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting, dance and music, the disciplines a celebrity entertainer masters, are collectively called the performing arts.

clue.text: Maybe switch round terms of reference

indicators.note: turning something round makes it face the opposite way, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: a timer is one example of a switch, hence 'maybe'

explanation.surface: Perhaps the brief should be swapped around, a committee member suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A remit is the scope of responsibility given to a body, the same thing as its terms of reference.

clue.text: Rotten, perhaps, virtually weak chair king occupies

indicators.note: virtually means almost but not quite, so the word loses its final letter
to occupy is to sit inside a space, so this letter goes within the others

blocks.note: puny means feeble
a rocker is a rocking chair
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A frail monarch sits in an almost-collapsing armchair, judged rotten by onlookers.
explanation.walkthrough: The king slots in between the shortened weak word and the chair. Johnny Rotten was the singer of the Sex Pistols.
explanation.definitionFit: Johnny Rotten fronted the Sex Pistols, so he is an example of a punk musician, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Release pressure from tyre in an angry manner

indicators.note: releasing something lets it go, so the named letter is let out of the word

blocks.note: P is the symbol for pressure in physics
a cross-ply tyre has its cords laid diagonally

explanation.surface: A frustrated driver lets the air out of a tyre in a temper.
explanation.walkthrough: Letting air out of a tyre is literal deflation in the surface; here only the letter for pressure is let out.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross means irritated or annoyed, so the adverb crossly describes acting irritably.

clue.text: Belittle revolutionary writer defending article

indicators.note: a defender stands around what is protected, so these letters enclose the article

blocks.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary
a pen is a writing implement
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Critics disparage a radical author who sticks up for a piece he wrote.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheapen someone is to degrade or lower them in esteem, a synonym of belittle.

clue.text: Replace old hat son wears

indicators.note: the son is wearing the hat, so the hat goes around him

blocks.note: old hat means unfashionable, or out
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A boy dons his father's battered old hat, which needs swapping for a new one.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust someone is to remove them from a position, often so another can take their place.

clue.text: They're tied up with criminal cases involving B&B, losing time

indicators.note: losing something means going without it, so a letter is dropped
criminal means crooked, so the word beside it is bent out of order
involving means taking in, so these letters wrap around the other part

blocks.note: taken as written
a bed and breakfast is a modest hotel
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Detectives are kept busy with crooked dealings at a guesthouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tied up' looks like 'busy' but is literal. The hotel loses its T before being wrapped by the rearranged cases.
explanation.definitionFit: Laces on shoes are knotted when worn, so the answer is literally things that get tied.

clue.text: Reportedly what a small sheep means to farmer in county

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by how the phrase is spoken

blocks.clueFragment: what a small sheep means to farmer
blocks.note: a small sheep carries less wool, so there is less work for the farmer with the clippers

explanation.surface: A shepherd ponders what owning a little ewe means for a farm in the Midlands.
explanation.walkthrough: The county name is pronounced roughly LESTER-sher, close to the spoken phrase. Leicestershire is an English county in the East Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Leicestershire is one of the English shire counties, centred on the city of Leicester.

clue.text: Prominent classical feature of flower inspiring country name

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the flower takes the other letters inside it

blocks.note: a rose is a flower
Oman is a country in Arabia
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A notable flower gives a nation its name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prominent classical feature' is the definition: a Roman nose sticks out and comes from classical times.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman nose has a high bridge like those on classical statues, so it is a prominent facial feature.

clue.text: Goes off to return drug cache

indicators.note: returning means going back the way one came, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: food that goes off rots
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A user leaves to fetch their hidden stash of narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden supply put away for later, which is a store.

clue.text: Craft using clay wingless animal

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its two ends, so both outer letters are clipped off

blocks.note: pottery is the craft of shaping clay

explanation.surface: A clay model of a creature that has no wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' suggests a boat or vessel, but it is the art of working clay.
explanation.definitionFit: An otter is a semi-aquatic mammal of the weasel family, so it is an animal.

clue.text: Weakens regiment guarding palace primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is wanted
guards stand around what they protect, so the regiment encloses the letter

blocks.note: the SAS is the Special Air Service regiment
the opening letter of palace

explanation.surface: Soldiers standing guard at a royal residence are growing tired.
explanation.definitionFit: To sap is to drain strength gradually, so saps means weakens.

clue.text: Not quite building coalition of parties

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the word stops before its final letter

blocks.note: a block is a large building, as in a block of flats

explanation.surface: An unfinished construction project is like an unstable political alliance.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is a group of nations or political parties allied for a common purpose.

clue.text: One stopping boss recently almost finding one-room property

indicators.note: almost means nearly but not entirely, so the final letter goes
stopping a gap means plugging it, so this letter fills a space between the other parts

blocks.note: a boss is a raised knob or stud, as on a shield
the Roman numeral for one
of late means recently

explanation.surface: Someone halts their manager's recent hunt for a bedsit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' suggests a manager, but here it is an ornamental knob. A studio flat is what Americans call a studio apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio flat combines living, sleeping and cooking in a single room, so it is a one-room property.

clue.text: Parody shriek by La bohème character

blocks.note: Mimì is the heroine of Puccini's opera
a shriek is a cry

explanation.surface: A send-up of an opera singer's scream as the consumptive heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' means next to: the shriek comes beside the opera character.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimicry is imitation, often comic, which is what a parody is.

clue.text: Giving authority to fellow on Tinder?

blocks.note: a fellow is a man
Tinder is a dating app, so someone on it is dating

explanation.surface: A man using a dating app is being given official power.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the Tinder phrase is an example rather than a literal synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandating means officially authorising or empowering someone to act.

clue.text: Remarks on book reviews

blocks.note: first meaning: the verb, observes or spots
second meaning: the noun, critical write-ups in the press

explanation.surface: Comments on literary criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remarks' looks like a noun but is the verb sense, he remarks a change.
explanation.definitionFit: To remark is to observe, as notices does; a review of a book or play in a newspaper is called a notice.

clue.text: Buff colour of bread and nuts

blocks.note: nan or naan is Indian flatbread
nuts about something means keen on it

explanation.surface: A beige shade seen in a loaf with walnuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like food alongside bread, but it means enthusiastic.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a pale yellowish cotton cloth from Nanjing, and the name is used for its buff shade.

clue.text: Travelling anywhere without husband's a time to celebrate!

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the named letter is omitted
things that travel move about, so these letters move into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A wife free to go anywhere without her spouse finds it cause for a party!
explanation.definitionFit: The start of a new calendar year is marked with parties and fireworks, a holiday occasion.

clue.text: Way to welcome leading trendy dressmaker

indicators.note: welcoming a guest means taking them in, so these letters enclose the other part

blocks.note: a mode is a way or manner
leading means first, written 1ST

explanation.surface: A fashionable designer finds a method for greeting the top names.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading trendy' seems to go together, but 'leading' is wordplay and 'trendy' joins the dressmaker; 1ST is written with I for 1.
explanation.definitionFit: A modiste is a maker of fashionable dresses and hats, a stylish couturier.

clue.text: Rent, typically large amount, nurses watch it regularly rising

indicators.note: regularly means at fixed intervals, so every other letter is kept
to nurse is to hold close, so the large amount cradles the other letters
in a down entry rising means read from bottom to top, so the letters go backwards

blocks.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
the second, fourth and sixth letters of watch it
a sum is an amount

explanation.surface: A tenant watches their large monthly payment climb steadily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid to a landlord, but it is the Broadway show. Rent is Jonathan Larson's rock musical about struggling artists.
explanation.definitionFit: Rent is a famous stage show with songs, so it is an example of a musical, hence 'typically'.

clue.text: About to divide excellent nutritious fruit

indicators.note: dividing something means splitting it apart, so these letters sit in the middle of the other part

blocks.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI
ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A health food fan explains roughly how to split a superb berry.
explanation.definitionFit: The açaí berry from a Brazilian palm is promoted as a superfood rich in antioxidants.

clue.text: Members of Parliament left broadcast, cycling

indicators.note: cycling goes round and round, so a letter at the front comes round to the back

blocks.note: to broadcast seed is to sow it by scattering
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: MPs of the left take to the airwaves while out on their bikes.
explanation.walkthrough: A group of owls is called a parliament, so owls are its members. The first letter moves to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The collective noun for owls is a parliament, so each owl is literally a member of one.

clue.text: Comes across flipping enthralling black and white creatures

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so the phrase holds the answer within it
flipping something over turns it the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles on a gripping sight of black-and-white animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comes across' looks like the definition 'finds'; it is just the letters holding the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Orcas, or killer whales, are marine mammals with striking black and white markings.

clue.text: Charlie promises to pay to flee unstable island

indicators.note: fleeing means running away, so these letters leave the longer word

blocks.note: capricious means changeable or erratic
C is Charlie in the NATO alphabet
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A debtor called Charlie skips town for an island, leaving IOUs behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The deleted letters come off the end of the long word together.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples, off Italy's Sorrento peninsula.

clue.text: Dictator's narcissistic streak

indicators.note: a dictator here is one who dictates, speaking words for someone to write down

blocks.note: a narcissist is vain

explanation.surface: A tyrant's self-obsessed tendency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dictator' suggests a tyrant, but it means a person dictating aloud to a secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: A vein is a streak or seam, as in a vein of humour or ore in rock.

clue.text: Dropping racket, sorry to get beaten

indicators.note: dropping something means letting it fall away, so these letters are removed

blocks.note: a racket is a swindle or con
contrite means remorseful

explanation.surface: A tennis player throws down the racket, apologetic at losing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten' looks like defeated, but it is beaten as in a well-trodden path.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaten can mean worn by overuse, as in the beaten track; trite means overused and stale.

clue.text: Trees surrounding yard Alice put at random

indicators.note: at random means in no set order, so these letters are jumbled
surrounding means enclosing on all sides, so the jumbled letters go around the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: Alice planted trees haphazardly around the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Eucalypti is a plural of eucalyptus, the Australian gum tree.

clue.text: When everybody is out of military commander's vehicle

blocks.note: a general is a senior army officer
taken as written
a trike is a tricycle

explanation.surface: Everyone has climbed out of the commanding officer's car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' suggests absent or outside, but it means on strike. The 1926 General Strike in Britain is the famous example.
explanation.definitionFit: A general strike is a stoppage in which workers across all industries walk out at once.
